projects.t: Blink an LED
projects.what: Plug in, build TI's blink, then change the pattern.
projects.time: 3 min to blink, tools installed; first-time install about 30 min, 10 GB

projects.t: Print a message from the board on your computer
projects.what: Send text from the chip to a terminal on the Mac over the USB serial port, and loop it back.
projects.time: 10 min, tools installed; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Read a temperature sensor
projects.what: The board's thermistor or the chip's own sensor, printed every second.
projects.time: 30 min

projects.t: Show colors and read touch on a small screen
projects.what: A 3.5 inch SPI touch display on jumper wires, then a widget library on it.
projects.time: 1 evening; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Run an edge AI model on the chip
projects.what: A room-occupancy model, 636 to 32,836 weights, timed on the chip and checked against the test set.
projects.time: 1 evening; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Recognize a handwritten digit on the chip
projects.what: Draw a digit on a touch screen and a TI LaunchPad shows its answer. It takes 34 ms to read the digit; the demo waits half a second after you lift your finger before it looks. The same neural net reads its ten stored test digits on four boards.
projects.time: 1 evening; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Send a sensor reading to a phone over Bluetooth
projects.what: A beacon or TI's example advertising a reading to a phone or a Mac.
projects.time: 1 evening

projects.t: Add a low-power temperature sensor to Home Assistant
projects.what: A sleepy Zigbee sensor reporting a temperature into Home Assistant.
projects.time: about 10 min from build to the first reading; tools need about 13 GB, once

projects.t: Switch a board's LED from Home Assistant over Zigbee
projects.what: TI's on/off light example joined to Home Assistant through a Zigbee coordinator; Home Assistant switches the board's LED.
projects.time: about 20 min from build to a switch on 2026-10-05, not reproduced; tools need about 15 GB, once

projects.t: Send sensor readings over a sub-1 GHz radio
projects.what: Temperature, humidity and light from a Sensors BoosterPack, sent once a second at 915 MHz by a plain MSPM0 and a CC1407P radio plug-in, received by a CC1354P10 LaunchPad.
projects.time: an evening with two boards; the receiver build needs about 110 MB of SDK files

projects.t: See whether a room is occupied with a 60 GHz radar
projects.what: TI's 60 GHz radar board streams who is where in a room over USB with no setup; a script reads it and a timed test measures detection range, delay and false alarms.
projects.time: ten minutes to see frames; an afternoon for the timed test

projects.t: Send a sensor reading to Home Assistant over Wi-Fi
projects.what: A sensor reporting over Wi-Fi into Home Assistant.
projects.time: no timed run

projects.t: Update a board's firmware over the air
projects.what: An over-the-air firmware update from Home Assistant or a laptop.
projects.time: about 2 min to build

projects.t: A Matter light in Apple Home
projects.what: Switch the CC35X1's red LED from Apple Home over Wi-Fi.
projects.time: About 20 min after host setup (estimate)

projects.t: Measure how fast a chip runs (CoreMark)
projects.what: CoreMark and the rest of the suite, the same source on every board, by compiler and operating system.
projects.time: 85 s to rerun; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: How fast a chip reacts to a signal
projects.what: Interrupt latency, and a sensor-to-output control step like a motor controller runs.
projects.time: 1 evening; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Measure a board's current draw, for battery life
projects.what: Running and STANDBY current measured through the debug probe of a second board. Coin-cell life is not measured.
projects.time: 1 evening

projects.t: Build and flash from the terminal in one command
projects.what: One make command and one flash command, no window.
projects.time: 5 min once the tools are installed (12 GB, once)

projects.t: Run the Zephyr real-time operating system
projects.what: Zephyr's blink from the command line, on the upstream board or on an out-of-tree board file.
projects.time: about 3 min with this repo's script; 2 GB download, nothing else to install

projects.t: Run the FreeRTOS real-time operating system
projects.what: FreeRTOS tasks on a chip with no TI example, and how many fit.
projects.time: 1 evening; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Run Arduino's own sketches on a TI chip
projects.what: The Arduino API on a TI chip, through the Zephyr-based Arduino core or through this repository's portability layer.
projects.time: about 80 s a build after a one-time setup of about 5 GB of tools

projects.t: Program a TI chip in Python (MicroPython)
projects.what: MicroPython on a TI chip, through upstream MicroPython's own Zephyr port.
projects.time: about 3 minutes a build after a one-time setup of about 5 GB of tools

projects.t: Configure a TI radio chip with ESPHome
projects.what: ESPHome's YAML configuration running on a TI radio chip, built and flashed with ESPHome's own commands.
projects.time: about 1 min from esphome compile to a running device on the LP-EM-CC2755P10: 35 s build, 15 s upload, 5.7 to 6.3 s to join

projects.t: Run a vision model on a Linux board's AI accelerator
projects.what: TI's SK-TDA4VM starter kit on its Edge AI Linux: boot it, run TI's model zoo on the C7x accelerator, decode video into a model with no CPU copy, and measure what the two Arm cores are left doing.
projects.time: one evening; 62 min from a working serial console to the first login, 15 GB on a second computer

projects.t: Detect a smoke alarm's beeps with a microphone
projects.what: Try an experimental alarm-pattern detector on the LP-MSPM0G5187. It reported smoke-alarm sounds played through a laptop speaker; learning has run over USB. Detection and learning with a real alarm remain untested.
projects.time: 1 evening; tools need 12 GB free, once

projects.t: Spin a brushless motor
projects.what: A three-phase brushless motor with Hall sensors, spun three ways from one LaunchPad and one driver board: six-step on the Halls, field-oriented control (FOC) on the Halls, and FOC with the Halls out of the control loop.
projects.time: 1 evening for six-step; a day for the FOC versions; tools need about 10 GB, once

projects.t: Asset tracking over Bluetooth
projects.what: A machine's motor MCU sends run events, run time and overcurrent trips to a Bluetooth tag. A Wi-Fi hub collects every machine in range and serves a phone app, no internet. An edge AI model on the tag classifies each event.
projects.time: an afternoon with two boards

projects.t: Make a Bluetooth game controller from a LaunchPad
projects.what: The LaunchPad kit's two buttons become buttons 1 and 2 of a Bluetooth LE game controller. A Mac lists it under Game Controllers with no driver, and a browser page shows the presses (checked by eye in Chrome).
projects.time: 1 evening (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Jack-o'-Lantern Jukebox
projects.what: A LaunchPad plays a Halloween music and light show from a power bank: orchestra and organ recordings, synth songs and scare sounds through the BOOSTXL-AUDIO, with the board's RGB LED following the music.
projects.time: under an hour once the tools are installed (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Doom on a TI board
projects.what: The Doom engine on two Cortex-M33 kits with the rp2040-doom design, and on the AM62L with a frame-buffer port.
projects.time: about an hour once the tools are installed (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Retro games on a TI LaunchPad
projects.what: A Game Boy emulator, Arduboy games, 2048, Minesweeper, CHIP-8 and a ZX Spectrum on LaunchPad screens.
projects.time: under an hour per game once the tools are installed (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Post-quantum on every board
projects.what: ML-KEM-768 key exchange and ML-DSA-44 signatures, the same portable C, on five TI boards; the full key exchange with a Mac on the CC1354P10.
projects.time: an hour once the tools are installed (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: A DNS ad blocker on a Wi-Fi board
projects.what: A DNS server on the LP-EM-CC35X1 that answers 0.0.0.0 for 71,492 blocklisted names and forwards the rest.
projects.time: about half an hour (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: A Lisp prompt on a LaunchPad
projects.what: uLisp 4.9a on the LP-MSPM0G5187, with a 160-line Arduino shim.
projects.time: about 10 minutes (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Audio BoosterPack on a LaunchPad
projects.what: A tone and a four-voice tune from the BOOSTXL-AUDIO's DAC on an LP-AM13E230, read back with the pack's microphone, plus a guitar tuner, spectrum, DTMF decoder and noise gate for the same microphone.
projects.time: about 20 minutes once the tools are installed (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Audio and video codecs on a LaunchPad
projects.what: LE Audio's LC3, Opus, MP3 and the Plaits synthesizer on an LP-MSPM33C321A, MP3 on an LP-MSPM0G3519, and H.264 video on the LP-MSPM33C321A and LP-AM13E230, each checked frame by frame against a Mac build.
projects.time: about 20 minutes per codec once the tools are installed (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Walkie-talkie over a 915 MHz radio
projects.what: A spoken line goes from a Mac over a 915 MHz radio link between two LaunchPad kits and plays back the same, one way.
projects.time: an afternoon, mostly the CC1354P10 build (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Sub-1 GHz home radio demos
projects.what: A fox hunt, a key finder and a mailbox, doorbell, panic and keep-close tag set, each run over 915 MHz between an LP-MSPM0G5187 with a CC1407P radio and an LP-CC1354P10-1.
projects.time: an afternoon, mostly the CC1354P10 build (estimate, not timed)

projects.t: Button, knob and dimmer
projects.what: Read the board's own S2 button, read a knob with the analog-to-digital converter, and dim an LED with PWM, in one short build on a breadboard.
projects.time: One sitting, not yet timed

projects.t: Traffic light, police strobe and a buzzer tune
projects.what: Three LEDs run a traffic light, a two-button reaction game times your press, and a passive buzzer plays a 14-note melody, in a loop.
projects.time: One sitting, not yet timed

projects.t: Parking sensor
projects.what: An ultrasonic distance sensor measures how far away your hand or a wall is, and a buzzer beeps faster as the distance shrinks.
projects.time: One sitting, not yet timed

projects.t: Room weather station
projects.what: A DHT11 sensor reads temperature and humidity and a 0.96 inch OLED shows them; the Sensors BoosterPack's own humidity sensor can sit beside it.
projects.time: One evening, not yet timed

projects.t: Servo on a knob, then pan and tilt
projects.what: A knob sets the angle of a servo; a second knob and a second servo make a pan and tilt neck.
projects.time: One sitting, not yet timed

projects.t: Motion alarm with a counter
projects.what: A PIR motion sensor sets off a buzzer, and a four-digit display counts each time something moves in front of it.
projects.time: One sitting, not yet timed

projects.t: Motor speed from a knob
projects.what: A rotary knob sets the speed and direction of a small DC motor through a DRV8833 motor driver, with the speed shown on a four-digit display.
projects.time: One evening, not yet timed

projects.t: Addressable LED ring and strip
projects.what: An 8-LED ring from the Freenove kit runs a rainbow and a few effects, then a 60-LED strip runs the same effects.
projects.time: One evening, not yet timed

projects.t: Relay lamp from a button
projects.what: A push button switches a 12 V lamp through a relay, the first step toward a lamp that a phone or Home Assistant can switch.
projects.time: One evening, not yet timed

projects.t: Tilt level on an OLED
projects.what: An MPU6050 reads how the board is tilted and an OLED shows a bubble level that moves as you tilt it.
projects.time: One evening, not yet timed

projects.t: Obstacle-avoiding robot car
projects.what: A two-wheeled robot drives forward, senses an obstacle with an ultrasonic sensor, and turns away.
projects.time: Two or three sittings, not yet timed

projects.t: Handheld touch screen dashboard
projects.what: A 3.5 inch touch panel shows a small dashboard of the board's own readings and a few tiles you tap, drawn with LVGL.
projects.time: Two or three sittings, not yet timed

projects.t: A voice assistant on a LaunchPad
projects.what: Sparky, a voice assistant on the LP-EM-CC35X1 with the Audio BoosterPack: you ask, a server on your network answers, and the board speaks. An optional 3.5 inch touch screen adds four looks and kids' games.
projects.time: a day: the server, the build and the programming; the Hey Sparky model needs your own training

projects.t: Holiday lights: first light with a button
projects.what: A 12-pixel WS2812B ring runs a few holiday light modes on an LP-MSPM0G3507. The board's S2 button steps through the modes and an optional knob sets the brightness.
projects.time: One evening, not yet timed
